implementation.scope: Only explicit near-SoM connector intent backed by an existing hard near_max term. Ordinary anchors take a fast no-op path.
implementation.geometry: For each selected shape, intersect the occupancy search window with the necessary translation envelope of its actual pad hull around the fixed SoM connector rectangle. Apply the same rule to single-shape seating, multi-shape trials and displaced-block reseating.
implementation.semantics: Necessary rectangular prefilter only. Corners can exceed Euclidean distance. All final hard terms, geometry and physical checks remain authoritative; no gate bound changed.
implementation.numerics: Validate finite ordered rectangles, nonnegative distance/guard, and finite output. Use the existing occupancy cell as a conservative search-only guard against cancellation on closed grid boundaries. A demonstrated counterexample had target=.1, moving right edge=.3, distance=2, grid x=-2.2: direct gap arithmetic accepts exactly 2 while the unguarded rearranged lower bound is -2.1999999999999997. The guard retains this candidate without changing its final acceptance limit.

tests.name: native_floorplan_contracts
tests.coverage: Asymmetric pad extents; independent Euclidean-gap oracle over 3111 translations; closed zero-distance point bounds; actual cancellation witness; intentionally insufficient rectangular corner condition; negative/nonfinite/overflow rejection; existing both-board geometry, repeatability and publication contracts.

smaller_screen.before: Late legalizer contradiction between near-SoM upper bound and USB-JTAG separation lower bound.
smaller_screen.after: Early interior_seating rejection at usb_jtag after proximity-domain seating of the constrained termination group.

limits: No new board promoted and no smaller-dimension claim. Runtime samples are short local screens, not statistically established general speedups or matched Python timings. Full qualification remains tied to its recorded revision; successful geometry was independently matched.
